THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The insurer is in appeal challenging the compensation awarded to a 10 year old boy who met with an accident.
The doctor has assessed 20% disability to the limb where the claimant has suffered fracture of tibia.

While determining the compensation, the Tribunal has taken 20% disability to the whole body and applying the ratio laid down in the case of Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, the National Insurance Company Limited and Another [AIR 2014 SC 736], the tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3.00 lakhs.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, the National Insurance Company Limited and Another [AIR 2014 SC 736]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In addition to that compensation is also awarded under other heads.

2. Smt Preethi Shashank, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/insurer would contend that the Tribunal erred in taking 20% as the disability to the whole body given the fact that the doctor himself has stated that the claimant has suffered 20% disability to the affected limb.
That being the case, it is her contention that 1/3 of the total disability assessed to the particular limb has to be taken as the disability to the whole body to determine the compensation.

3. This Court has perused the records made available by the learned counsel for the insurer and the doctor's certificate at Ex.P.12 would reveal that the doctor has certified that the claimant has suffered 20% disability to the affected right lower limb.
That being the position, the Tribunal was in error in taking the disability at 20% to the whole body to determine the compensation.

It has to be noticed that in the cross examination the doctor who has been examined on behalf of the claimant has stated that he is not in a position to assess the disability to the whole body.

The relevant portion of the cross examination reads as under:
FU v v At zz U vAi U U    DU.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This being the position, the Tribunal was in error in assessing the disability at 20% to the whole body to determine the compensation.
4. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the insurer the Tribunal at the most ought to have taken 8% as the disability at the most to the whole body.

That being the position, applying the ratio laid down in the case of Master Mallikarjun referred supra, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of 'pain and suffering', loss of amenities in life, inconvenience.
5. Compensation under the head of 'medical expenses' awarded at Rs.58,000/- is supported by documents, therefore, it does not require any modification.

6. However, further compensation under the heads grevious injuries, pain and suffering at Rs.10,000/- and Rs.5,000/- towards grevious injuries and towards conveyance, attendant,
nourishment and miscellaneous charges have to be excluded in view of the law laid down in the case of Master Mallikarjun referred supra.
7.

However, it is to be noticed that compensation is not awarded for loss of income during the laid-up period and also for the discomfort and inconvenience caused to the parents on account of the injuries sustained by the minor.
8. Accident is of the year 2015.
As per the chart prepared by the High Court Legal Services Authority, notional income should be taken at Rs.8,000/- per month.
9. Taking 2 months as the loss of earnings during the laid-up period, Rs.16,000/- is to be awarded under the head of 'loss of income during the laid-up period by the claimant.
10. Accordingly, the compensation payable would be Rs.1,74,000/-.
11. The appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award are modified.
The claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,74,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
In all other aspects, the award of the Tribunal is undisturbed.
12. It is stated that 50% of the compensation amount deposited by the insurer is withdrawn.
13. If the amount is withdrawn by the claimant, the insurer shall satisfy the remaining portion of the award.
Amount in deposit if any be transmitted to the Tribunal.
